title: Atrichia with Papular Lesions in a Chinese Family Caused by Novel Compound Heterozygous Mutations and Literature Review
abstract: <b><i>Background:</i></b> Congenital atrichia with papular lesions (APL) is characterized by complete absence of body hair shortly after birth, along with papules, and caused by mutations in the hairless gene <i>(HR)</i>. <b><i>Objective:</i></b> To investigate whether APL with <i>HR</i> mutations might also be found among patients in non-consanguineous Chinese families and to discuss the phenotypic variations with the same mutations. <b><i>Methods:</i></b> DNA sequencing of the <i>HR</i> was performed in the Chinese pedigree and in 100 controls. <b><i>Results:</i></b> A nonsense mutation c.T2265A in the patient and his father as well as a 2bp deletion (3482delCT) in the patient and his mother were detected. <b><i>Conclusion:</i></b> Our study identified the first mutation in exon 10 in <i>HR</i> as well as the second novel compound heterozygous mutations in a Chinese family, also adding new variants to the knowledge of <i>HR</i> mutations in APL. Phenotypic heterogeneity in congenital atrichia might be subject to the founder genes or modifier genes.
